extracted_data.title: OOS Assay Result for Metformin Hydrochloride API Batch MFH-2609-042
extracted_data.description: During routine QC testing of Batch MFH-2609-042, an Out-of-Specification (OOS) result was observed for the Assay parameter. The result obtained was 96.5%, which is below the lower limit of 98.0%. The analysis was repeated by a second analyst using the same sample preparation, and a result of 96.7% was obtained, confirming the initial OOS finding. The batch has been quarantined, and a hold label was applied. The production team has been notified to halt any further processing or packaging of the related intermediate batches until the root cause is identified.
extracted_data.aiExplanation: The deviation involves a critical OOS result for the Assay parameter of the primary active ingredient, which directly impacts product quality and release. The severity is Critical because the batch cannot be released and requires immediate investigation and quarantine.

extracted_text:
Deviation / Incident Report
Report Date: 2026-09-24
Reported By: John Doe, Quality Assurance
1. Basic Information
Site / Plant: API Manufacturing Unit
Date of Occurrence: 2026-09-23
Source of Deviation: Quality Control (QC)
Related Product / Material: Metformin Hydrochloride API
Batch / Lot Number: MFH-2609-042
2. Deviation Details
Description of Event:
During routine QC testing of Batch MFH-2609-042, an Out-of-Specification (OOS) result was observed for the
Assay parameter. The result obtained was 96.5%, which is below the lower limit of 98.0%. The analysis was
repeated by a second analyst using the same sample preparation, and a result of 96.7% was obtained,
confirming the initial OOS finding.
Immediate actions taken:
The batch has been quarantined, and a hold label was applied. The production team has been notified to halt
any further processing or packaging of the related intermediate batches until the root cause is identified.
3. Initial Assessment
Initial Impact Assessment: The impact is expected to be High as this concerns the primary active ingredient
and fails the critical Assay specification, meaning the batch cannot be released.
Initial Severity: Critical
